data.summary: The plan front‑loads the student’s weak units (2, 4, 6) with focused live classes and targeted practice, then moves through the remaining units while keeping a steady mix of concept work, free‑response drills, and timed practice. The final week is dedicated to mixed review and timed exam‑style problems to consolidate knowledge and build stamina.

weeks.focus: Build foundational differentiation skills (Unit 2) and attend live Class 11300.
tasks: Watch the recorded lecture for Class 11300 and take concise notes on average vs. instantaneous rate.
Do 12 free‑response questions on defining the derivative and using derivative notation; check answers with the scoring guide.
Complete 8 derivative estimation problems from a textbook table; verify with calculator.
Create a one‑page summary sheet of the Power Rule with example problems.

weeks.focus: Master limits and continuity (Unit 1) and begin composite differentiation.
tasks: Solve 10 limit problems involving algebraic manipulation and tables; write a brief justification for each.
Graph three functions and estimate limits from the graphs; compare with analytic results.
Practice the Chain Rule on 6 composite functions; record each step on paper.
Do 5 FRQs that combine limits with the definition of the derivative.

weeks.focus: Implicit, inverse functions, and related differentiation techniques (Unit 3).
tasks: Complete 8 implicit differentiation problems, then solve for dy/dx explicitly.
Work through 6 inverse function differentiation examples, checking with the inverse function theorem.
Practice differentiating inverse trigonometric functions in 5 problems.
Take a timed 15‑minute mini‑quiz covering all three sub‑topics.

weeks.focus: Contextual applications of differentiation (Unit 4) and attend live Class 11301.
tasks: Review notes from Class 11301; write a one‑sentence interpretation for each derivative context.
Solve 4 related‑rates problems involving motion and 4 problems involving non‑motion rates.
Create a concept map linking position, velocity, acceleration, and rates of change.
Do 6 FRQs that require setting up and solving a related‑rates equation; self‑grade with the rubric.
Apply the Mean Value Theorem to 4 functions; write the theorem statement each time.
Identify critical points and classify extrema for 6 different functions using the First Derivative Test.
Create a table of intervals of increase/decrease for 5 functions and verify with graphs.
Complete a mixed‑practice set of 8 FRQs covering all Unit 5 concepts.

weeks.focus: Integration fundamentals (Unit 6) and attend live Class 11302.
tasks: Review Class 11302 notes; summarize the connection between Riemann sums and definite integrals.
Compute 5 Riemann sum approximations (left, right, midpoint) for given functions.
Practice evaluating definite integrals using the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus in 6 problems.
Do 4 FRQs that require setting up an accumulation function and interpreting its meaning.

weeks.focus: Mixed review and timed practice for the whole AP Calculus AB exam.
tasks: Take a full‑length 90‑minute timed practice exam (all sections).
Mark the exam using the official scoring guide; note any recurring errors.
Review each incorrect problem, re‑doing it with a focus on the underlying concept.
Create a final cheat‑sheet of key formulas, theorems, and common FRQ strategies.

data.final_week_advice: After the review week, spend any remaining days doing additional timed sections, focusing on speed and accuracy. Rest well the night before the exam, and on test day bring your cheat‑sheet, a calculator, and confidence in the systematic problem‑solving process you have practiced.
